## Big Data Econometrics - Week 3 

# Exercise 4.3

We will be using factor models to see if we could have predicted large (recent) inflation.
We will use the monthly FRED data to conduct the analysis.

First, we have to import and retrieve the necessary data from the dataset using the given "Exercise_4_3_preparation.R" file.

```{r}
# import relevant packages
library(bootUR)
library(zoo)
library(dfms)
set.seed(333)

# use the given .r file to get the data
source("Exercise_4_3_preparation.R")

```

We can now start with the processing.

```{r}
# so we will take the cpi from the transformed data
infl <- as.numeric(fred_final$CPIAUCSL)
dates <- index(fred_final)
X_all <- as.matrix(fred_final[, colnames(fred_final) != "CPIAUCSL"])

plot(as.Date(dates), infl, type = "l", ylab = "cpi inflation (monthly)")
plot(fred_final$CPIAUCSL)
# initialise the horizons to use
h1 <- 1
h3 <- 3
h6 <- 6

```

Now we need to do the rolling window predictions.

```{r}
# set the parameters for the rolling window
window <- 240 # 20 years
h <- h1

n <- length(infl)
first <- as.yearmon("Jan 1995")
last <- as.yearmon("Dec 2014")
lastlast <- as.yearmon("Dec 2021")

firstind <- max(which(dates <= first))
lastind <- max(which(dates <= last))
lastlastind <- max(which(dates <= lastlast))

endlast <- lastlastind - h # the final window's start index
endindices <- lastind:lastlastind 

```

Now do th emodel 

```{r}
forecast <- function(u = infl, v = X_all) {
  # window_data arrives as a mini zoo object
  model <- lm(u ~ v)
  
  # Predict 1 step ahead of this specific window's end date
  next_day <- max(v) + 1
  return(predict(model, newdata = data.frame(window = next_day)))
}

#rollapply(fred_final, width = 10, FUN = forecast, align = "right", by.column = TRUE)

```


```{r}
# initialise all necessary aspects for the rolling window
dates <- index(fred_final)
x_all <- as.matrix(fred_final[, colnames(fred_final) != "CPIAUCSL"])


# set the training range
train_end_date <- as.yearmon("Dec 2014")
train_idx      <- which(dates <= train_end_date)

# set the training dates
xtrain <- x_all[train_idx,]


ic <- ICr(xtrain, max.r = 20)
print(ic)       # shows the criteria for each number of factors
plot(ic)        # scree plot / IC curves
ic$r.star       # optimal number of factors according to IC1, IC2, IC3

r <- ic$r.star[1]   # use IC1 (check the printout; pick whichever you prefer)
r
```


# Exercise 5.3

In this exercise we try to extract underlying factors for student stress.

Start with instantiating everything we need.

```{r}
#install.packages(c("psych", "glmnet", "corrplot", "ggplot2", "GPArotation"))
library(glmnet)
library(ggplot2)
library(dfms)

library(corrplot)
library(psych)
set.seed(333)

# import data
stress_data <- read.csv("StressLevelDataset.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# check what the structure is like
str(stress_data)
cat("Missing values in dataset:", sum(is.na(stress_data)), "\n")

```

Now we set up the system such that we separate the dependent variable (target var.) and the predictors

```{r}
yvar <- "academic_performance"

y <- stress_data[[yvar]]
X <- stress_data[, names(stress_data) != yvar]

# Standardize predictors for PCA/Factor Analysis
Xmat <- as.matrix(X)
Xscaled <- scale(Xmat)

n <- nrow(X)
p <- ncol(X)

```

Now we can explore the data to find the PC and estimate the factors.

```{r}
# see what we get from the information criteria
ic <- ICr(Xscaled, max.r = min(20, ncol(X) - 1))
plot(ic)
ic$r.star

# then look at the scree plot
pca <-  prcomp(Xscaled, center = FALSE, scale. = FALSE)
pca

# visualise the change in residual variance
screeplot(pca, npcs = 20, type = "lines", main = "Scree plot")

```

The information criteria gives 19 (the max), but I would choose 3 from the scree plot (based on the lack of improvement after that).
Now continue to the getting the F matrix

```{r}
# set the chosen r value
r <- 3
F_hat <- pca$x[, 1:r, drop = FALSE]
colnames(F_hat) <- paste0("F", 1:r)

# look at the rotation matrix to find the loadings for the factors
loadingsF <- pca$rotation[, 1:r, drop = FALSE]
loadingsF

```
The loadings seem to make sense. The first factor shows that there are positive loadings between self-esteem, sleep_quality, safety, etc. These are all reasonable things that would drive one to have "good" grades.

Now do the prediction/forecasting and compare performance.

```{r}
# do forecasting on different training sets (the types mentioned in the exercise)
train_idx <- sample(1:n, size = 0.7 * n)
test_idx  <- setdiff(1:n, train_idx)

y_train <- y[train_idx]
y_test  <- y[test_idx]

# original features
X_train <- Xscaled[train_idx, ]
X_test  <- Xscaled[test_idx, ]

# extracted factors
F_train <- F_hat[train_idx, ]
F_test  <- F_hat[test_idx, ]

# hybrid data (original features + factors)
X_hybrid_train <- cbind(X_train, F_train)
X_hybrid_test  <- cbind(X_test, F_test)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fit Original Features Only (Lasso & Ridge)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# lasso (alpha = 1)
cv_lasso_orig <- cv.glmnet(X_train, y_train, alpha = 1)
pred_m1_lasso <- predict(cv_lasso_orig, s = "lambda.min", newx = X_test)
mspe_m1_lasso <- mean((y_test - as.vector(pred_m1_lasso))^2)

# ridge (alpha = 0)
cv_ridge_orig <- cv.glmnet(X_train, y_train, alpha = 0)
pred_m1_ridge <- predict(cv_ridge_orig, s = "lambda.min", newx = X_test)
mspe_m1_ridge <- mean((y_test - as.vector(pred_m1_ridge))^2)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fit Factors Only (OLS)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
fit_factors <- lm(y_train ~ ., data = as.data.frame(F_train))
pred_m2 <- predict(fit_factors, newdata = as.data.frame(F_test))
mspe_m2 <- mean((y_test - pred_m1)^2)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fit Hybrid (Factors + Original Features, Elastic Net / Lasso)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
cv_hybrid_lasso <- cv.glmnet(X_hybrid_train, y_train, alpha = 1)
pred_m3_hybrid <- predict(cv_hybrid_lasso, s = "lambda.min", newx = X_hybrid_test)
mspe_m3_hybrid <- mean((y_test - as.vector(pred_m3_hybrid))^2)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Summary of Results
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
results_table <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Original Features (Lasso)", 
            "Original Features (Ridge)",
            "Factors Only (OLS)", 
            "Hybrid: Features + Factors (Lasso)"),
  Test_MSPE = c(mspe_m1, mspe_m2_lasso, mspe_m2_ridge, mspe_m3_hybrid),
  Relative_to_Factors = c(1.00, mspe_m2_lasso / mspe_m1, 
                          mspe_m2_ridge / mspe_m1, mspe_m3_hybrid / mspe_m1)
)

print((results_table))
```

Now visualise the performances.

```{r}
# Comparison Plot of Test Prediction Errors (MSPE)
ggplot(results_table, aes(x = reorder(Model, Test_MSPE), y = Test_MSPE, fill = Model)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.55, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(Test_MSPE, 4)), vjust = -0.4, size = 3.8) +
  labs(
    title = "Academic Performance Prediction: Test MSPE Comparison",
    x = "Model Specification",
    y = "Mean Squared Prediction Error (MSPE)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 15, hjust = 1))
```

# alternative by gemini

```{r}
# 1. Prepare data (excluding academic performance)
k_max <- min(10, p - 1)  # Maximum candidate factors to check

# 2. Compute Eigen-decomposition of X'X (slide formula for n > p)
XtX <- t(Xmat) %*% Xmat
eig <- eigen(XtX)

eigen_values  <- eig$values
eigen_vectors <- eig$vectors  # Lambda_hat matrix

# 3. Calculate V(k), R^2(k), and Bai & Ng Criteria for k = 0, ..., k_max
V_k <- numeric(k_max + 1)
R2_k <- numeric(k_max + 1)

# k = 0 (no factors, residual is X itself)
V_k[1]  <- sum(X^2) / (n * p)  # Equals 1 due to standardization
R2_k[1] <- 0

# Loop for k = 1 to k_max
for (k in 1:k_max) {
  # Loadings: sqrt(p) * eigenvectors so that Lambda'Lambda / p = I_k
  Lambda_k <- eigen_vectors[, 1:k, drop = FALSE] * sqrt(p)
  
  # Factor estimates: F_hat = X * Lambda_hat / p
  F_k <- (Xmat %*% Lambda_k) / p
  
  # Residuals: X - F_hat * Lambda_hat'
  E_k <- Xmat - F_k %*% t(Lambda_k)
  
  V_k[k + 1]  <- sum(E_k^2) / (n * p)
  R2_k[k + 1] <- 1 - V_k[k + 1]
}

# 4. Penalty functions from the slides
g1 <- ((n + p) / (n * p)) * log((n * p) / (n + p))
g2 <- ((n + p) / (n * p)) * log(min(n, p))
g3 <- log(min(n, p)) / min(n, p)

sigma_nu2 <- V_k[k_max + 1]  # V(k_max)
k_grid <- 0:k_max

# Compute Information Criteria tables
IC1 <- log(V_k) + k_grid * g1
IC2 <- log(V_k) + k_grid * g2
IC3 <- log(V_k) + k_grid * g3

PC1 <- V_k + k_grid * sigma_nu2 * g1
PC2 <- V_k + k_grid * sigma_nu2 * g2
PC3 <- V_k + k_grid * sigma_nu2 * g3

ic_summary <- data.frame(
  k = k_grid,
  V_k = round(V_k, 4),
  R2 = round(R2_k, 4),
  Delta_R2 = c(0, round(diff(R2_k), 4)),
  IC1 = round(IC1, 4),
  IC2 = round(IC2, 4),
  IC3 = round(IC3, 4),
  PC1 = round(PC1, 4),
  PC2 = round(PC2, 4),
  PC3 = round(PC3, 4)
)
print(ic_summary)

# Identify optimal r for each criterion (ignoring k=0)
r_hat_IC1 <- which.min(IC1[-1])
r_hat_IC2 <- which.min(IC2[-1])
r_hat_IC3 <- which.min(IC3[-1])
cat(sprintf("\nOptimal number of factors selected:\nIC1: %d | IC2: %d | IC3: %d\n", 
            r_hat_IC1, r_hat_IC2, r_hat_IC3))
```

```{r}
# Replicate Smeekes Slide Scree Plot
delta_R2 <- diff(R2_k)

plot(1:k_max, delta_R2, type = "b", pch = 19, col = "black",
     xlab = "k", ylab = expression(R^2*(k) - R^2*(k-1)),
     main = "Scree Plot of Marginal Explained Variance",
     ylim = c(0, max(delta_R2) * 1.1))
# Add red vertical line at r_hat from IC
abline(v = r_hat_IC2, col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
legend("topright", legend = c(expression(Delta*R^2), expression(hat(r)[IC])),
       col = c("black", "red"), lty = c(1, 2), pch = c(19, NA), lwd = c(1, 2))
```

```{r}
r_chosen <- r_hat_IC2

# Extract eigenvectors corresponding to r largest eigenvalues
Lambda_hat <- eigen_vectors[, 1:r_chosen, drop = FALSE] * sqrt(p)
colnames(Lambda_hat) <- paste0("Factor_", 1:r_chosen)
rownames(Lambda_hat) <- colnames(X)

# Calculate factor matrix: F_hat = X * Lambda_hat / p (dimension: n x r)
F_hat <- (Xmat %*% Lambda_hat) / p
colnames(F_hat) <- paste0("Factor_", 1:r_chosen)

# Verify normalization from slides: F'F / n should be diagonal, Lambda'Lambda / p = I_r
cat("Check Lambda'Lambda / p (Identity):\n")
print(round(t(Lambda_hat) %*% Lambda_hat / p, 4))

head(F_hat)
```
```{r}
# do forecasting on different training sets (the types mentioned in the exercise)

y_test  <- y[test_idx]

pred_m2 <- predict(fit_factors, newdata = as.data.frame(F_test))
mspe_m2 <- mean((y_test - pred_m1)^2)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

  Test_MSPE = c(mspe_m1, mspe_m2_lasso, mspe_m2_ridge, mspe_m3_hybrid),
  Relative_to_Factors = c(1.00, mspe_m2_lasso / mspe_m1, 
                          mspe_m2_ridge / mspe_m1, mspe_m3_hybrid / mspe_m1)
)

print((results_table))
```
